q: How do I add an effect to a clip?
a: Find the effect in the Effects panel (Window ▸ Effects; `effects.list` lists them) and drag it onto a clip, or select clips and run `effects.apply`. Its controls appear in Effect Controls (Inspector in the Resolve workflow) under Motion, Opacity and Time Remapping (video) or Volume and Panner (audio). Effects run top to bottom; `effects.reset` restores defaults, `effects.remove` deletes it.

q: How do I keyframe an effect parameter?
a: Click the parameter's stopwatch (`effects.toggleAnimation`): a keyframe is set at the playhead, and every change at another time adds or changes one there. Move keyframes with `effects.moveKeyframe`, delete with `effects.deleteKeyframe`. Right-click a keyframe for its interpolation: Linear, Bezier, Auto Bezier, Continuous Bezier, Hold, Ease In, Ease Out.

q: When should I use linear keyframes?
a: Linear is constant speed and feels mechanical: right for fades, wipes and anything that should feel exact. Ease In / Ease Out and Bezier speed up and slow down for natural moves, zooms and titles; Hold jumps with no motion between keyframes.

q: How do I add a transition at an edit?
a: Park the playhead on the edit (or select clips) and apply the default video transition (`sequence.applyVideoTransition`) or audio crossfade (`sequence.applyAudioTransition`), or drag one from Effects ▸ Video / Audio Transitions onto the edit. Select it to change its length and alignment (`sequence.setTransition`) or delete it (`sequence.removeTransition`).

q: How do I change a transition's length?
a: Park the playhead on the edit (or select clips) and apply the default video transition (`sequence.applyVideoTransition`) or audio crossfade (`sequence.applyAudioTransition`), or drag one from Effects ▸ Video / Audio Transitions onto the edit. Select it to change its length and alignment (`sequence.setTransition`) or delete it (`sequence.removeTransition`).

q: How do I save an effect preset?
a: Select a clip, choose its effects in Effect Controls and Save Preset… (`presets.save`) with a name and a keyframe rule: Scale (stretch over the clip), Anchor to In Point / Out Point (keep distance from start or end), or none (values at the playhead only). Apply from Effects ▸ Presets or `presets.apply`; Motion, Opacity and Time Remapping in a preset replace the clip's own.

q: What does Motion in a preset do to the clip's own Motion?

q: In Premiere I'd keep presets in the Presets bin. Where are they here?
a: In the Effects panel's Presets bin (Effects ▸ Presets); `presets.list`, `presets.rename`, `presets.delete`, `presets.export` and `presets.import` manage them. For grades, use stills or a look pack instead.

q: What is a shader effect?
a: A shader effect is a small program that runs on the graphics card for every pixel of a clip. Revolution ships four in Video Effects ▸ User ▸ Stylize: Chromatic Aberration (coloured fringes growing towards the corners), Glitch (jumping split bands), VHS (wobble, bleeding, scanlines) and Light Leak (a drifting warm glow), and loads your own `.wgsl` files. Drag one onto a clip and set its controls in Effect Controls; they can be keyframed.

q: What can my shader code read?
a: Your `effect` function gets `px` (the pixel, centres at .5) and can use `size`, `time` (seconds since the clip started), `load(vec2<i32>)` and `sample(vec2<f32>)`. Colours are display colours (sRGB, 0–1) with transparency separate; Revolution converts around your code and keeps the result 0–1. Not allowed: your own bindings, entry points, storage or workgroup memory, names starting with `fx_`; at most 256 KB per file.

q: How is a shader effect's id made?
a: From the file name: `My Look.wgsl` becomes `user.my-look`. Files live in the Effects folder of Revolution's data folder (Open Effects Folder at the bottom of Video Effects ▸ User); click Reload (`effects.reloadUser`) after editing.

q: How do I use one of the shader recipes?
a: Open Effects Folder, make a text file such as `Soft Vignette.wgsl`, paste the recipe, click Reload; it appears under Video Effects ▸ User ▸ My looks. The Soft Vignette darkens edges: Size is where the darkening starts (0 middle, 1 corners) and Softness how gradually it fades in. Change a line, save and Reload to see the result.

q: What happens to a project when a shader effect file is missing?
a: The project keeps the effect with its values; Effect Controls shows a Missing effect row and the picture renders without it. Put the file back and click Reload.

q: Where is the transcript stored?
a: A transcript is the spoken words with each word's time, kept on the media item so every clip from that file shares it; the Text panel's Transcript tab shows the sequence's words in timeline order, grouped into paragraphs at pauses. Scripts can bring their own with `transcript.set`, read it with `transcript.inspect` and remove it with `transcript.delete`.

q: In Premiere I'd do text-based editing in the Text panel. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Window ▸ Text ▸ Transcript tab after Sequence ▸ Transcript ▸ Transcribe…: click words to jump, search, select a run of words and Extract (close the gap) or Lift (leave it). Every cut is a normal timeline edit you can trim afterwards.

q: Which Whisper model is the default?
a: whisper-base is the default, for most work; whisper-tiny makes quick drafts of clear speech but errs most on noise and accents; whisper-small handles hard audio, names and other languages at about four times base's time. All are multilingual, run locally and are listed by `transcript.models`; `transcript.downloadModel` gets one.

q: Which filler words does Remove Filler Words cut?
a: Both work from the sequence's transcript. Remove Pauses (`transcript.removePauses`) cuts silences longer than one second, keeping 0.15 s each side (`minSeconds`, `keepSeconds`); Remove Filler Words (`transcript.removeFillers`) cuts um, uh, erm, hmm and similar, or your own `fillers` list. Each is one undo step.

q: Where do captions live on the timeline?
a: Captions live on caption tracks above the video tracks (C1, C2…). By hand: Add New Caption Track… (`captions.newTrack`, Cmd+Alt+A: Subtitle, CEA-608, CEA-708 or Teletext) and Add Caption at Playhead (`captions.add`, Cmd+Alt+C, 3 s). Export a sidecar with File ▸ Export ▸ Captions… (SRT, WebVTT, SCC and others), or burn them in when exporting the video.

q: In Resolve I'd use a subtitle track. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Use a caption track: make one from the transcript (Create Captions from Transcript), import an .srt / .vtt / .scc file, or add a track and captions by hand; edit them in the Text panel's Captions tab and export SRT / WebVTT or burn them in.

q: Does the built-in TTS voice need a download?
a: The built-in voice works without a download; Natural voices (Kokoro-82M) are a one-time 336 MB download. Create (`tts.create`) writes `Narration <n>.wav`, imports it and places it at the playhead on a free audio track; it never overwrites a clip.
